name: 隠れや しぶ天 (Kakureya Shibuten (Shibu Ten))

claims.text: Offers a dedicated all-vegetable tempura course (7 pieces, ¥1,380 per person) explicitly aimed at vegan guests, using seasonal vegetables fried fresh to order rather than a modified version of a meat/seafood dish.

The core menu leans on agar-based anmitsu/mitsumame, azuki bean paste, matcha and warabimochi (bracken-starch, not wheat) — ingredients that are naturally wheat-free and, in some preparations, dairy-free — giving gluten-free and vegan-leaning diners a few plausible base choices to build from, even though no formal allergy protocol is documented.

name: からあげ 縁 浅草総本店 (Karaage Yukari Asakusa Sohonten)

claims.text: The chicken is marinated overnight in a secret sauce based on several types of soy sauce (shoyu) before frying, which contains wheat.

name: おかゆと麺のお店 粥餐庁 京王モール店（粥餐庁 新宿京王モール店） (Kayu Sanchin (Okayu to Men Kayu Sanchin) - S)

claims.text: Menu includes a dedicated multi-vegetable congee option with toppings such as lotus root, daikon, sweet potato, broccoli, and cherry tomato, giving vegetarian-leaning diners a clear plant-forward choice.

name: 北ノ醤油チーホー 水道橋店 (Kita no Shoyu Chi-Ho (Suidobashi))

claims.text: The ramen is built on a shoyu (soy sauce) broth; no gluten-free or wheat-free soy sauce alternative is mentioned in any source, so standard wheat-containing soy sauce should be assumed.
The broth and toppings are pork-based (minced pork stir-fried with garlic, pork back fat), with no vegetarian or vegan preparation mentioned.

name: 個室居酒屋 番屋 西新宿住友ビル店 (Koshitsu Izakaya Banya Nishi-Shinjuku Sumito)

claims.text: Rather than leaving vegetarian diners to piece together a meal from a meat- and fish-centric menu, the restaurant has a named, pre-set vegetarian course (8 dishes) explicitly described as free of meat, fish, and dairy, bookable when a vegetarian guest is part of a group.

name: 黒毛和牛 壱乃屋 浅草 (Kuroge Wagyu Ichinoya Asakusa)

claims.text: The house 'warishita' sauce is homemade from soy sauce and mirin — no gluten-free or wheat-free version is mentioned in any source found.
The entire menu centers on wagyu beef, egg yolk, and a beef-based dashi broth; no vegan, vegetarian, or plant-based option was found in any source.

name: 串揚げ かたやま (Kushiage Katayama)

claims.text: The restaurant's signature sauce lineup includes oroshi ponzu, a soy-sauce-based dressing, alongside original tartar sauces used across its 10-sauce tasting.
